The amplitude errors and phase angle errors of the IVDs with ratios from 2:1 to 256:1 have been measured by means of sampling method at frequencies ranging from 10 kHz to 100 kHz, and the measurement results are presented.

articleTitle: Evaluation of a continuously variable calculable capacitor
abstract: We report results using a new calculable capacitor. Its salient feature is continuous tunability over a range of 0.1 pF, enabling non-linearity testing of capacitance bridges.

articleTitle: Performance of the binary compensation unit for cryogenic current comparators
abstract: The binary compensation unit for PTB's resistance measurement bridge based on a cryogenic current comparator (CCC) is successfully operated for about three years now. In this contribution we focus on the stability of the compensation unit as investigated in a series of calibrations in 20-weeks intervals. As an example of the versatility, we present experimental data from the calibration of a 100 Ω normal resistor against the quantum Hall resistance (QHR) for different numbers-of-turns and compensation settings. The consistency of these results is a proof of the quality of this module.

articleTitle: Uncertainty analysis and evaluation of a WR-28 (26.5 to 40 GHz) millimeter-wave power standard
abstract: A new WR-28 (26.5 to 40 GHz) waveguide microcalorimeter has been recently developed at the National Institute of Metrology, China for a replacement of previous national primary power standard. The new microcalorimeter was preliminarily evaluated and successfully used to determine the effective efficiency of a transfer standard (i.e., thermistor mount). In this paper, measurements and evaluation of the new WR-28 microcalorimeter will be described, and uncertainty analysis for determining the effective efficiency of thermistor mount will be discussed briefly.

articleTitle: Mechanical aspects in mm-wave measurements
abstract: Mechanical deformations have a significant impact on electrical connections in mm-wave measurement systems. This paper presents constructional measures to improve the electrical stability of a coaxial measurement system for scattering parameters up to 110 GHz.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the automatic coaxial mechanical scanner for high-resistance measurement use
abstract: We have evaluated the automatic 4-terminal coaxial mechanical scanner for precise high-resistance measurement use. This scanner mechanically changes a set of 4-terminal BNC connections with coaxial cables by using servocontrolled motors. It was designed for impedance calibration use, and now we evaluated it for high-resistance measurement use. We compared the measured resistance ratio between the case with the scanner and without it in the range from 10 MΩ to 1 TΩ, and these result were agreed within about one tenth of the expanded uncertainty.

articleTitle: Feasibility study of electrical measurements of oscillating-magnet watt balance
abstract: New approach for Watt Balance is proposed in [1], where electrical measurements consisting of current causing the Lorentz's Force and Faraday's Voltage will be performed simultaneously. The general theory of the electrical measurements is established and demonstrated that the problem of the voltage drop due to stray resistance of the coil is intrinsically solved. Finite input resistance of the current source effect detrimentally the induced Faraday voltage when electrical measurements are performed simultaneously. Suggestion to solve this effect by applying spectral techniques and the results of numerical simulations made to assign uncertainty of the measured quantities are presented.

articleTitle: Voltage linearity evaluation for a high-speed digitizer adopted to a quantum sampling voltmeter
abstract: We report the linearity evaluation for a high-speed digitizer NI 5922, which is adopted to a quantum sampling voltmeter. The evaluation has been carried out for three units of the digitizer using a reference voltmeter with a 14-bit arbitrary waveform generator as a dummy voltage source. The three units show totally different behaviors in terms of the voltage linearity which might be described with different polynomial functions of input voltage. In the conference, we will present results of the linearity evaluation for the three units using a programmable Josephson voltage standard.

articleTitle: Uncertainty estimation for gallium nitride diode model based on VNA measurement at 5.8 GHz
abstract: This paper summarizes the uncertainty estimation for gallium nitride shottky diode based on vector network analyzer measurements at 5.8 GHz. The results were traceable to the metrology standard of S-parameter at NMIJ. Considering the uncertainty of the measurements, bias voltage must be applied over 2 V in measuring bias voltage dependence of reflection coefficient. The measurement uncertainty was propagated from reflection coefficient to impedance. As a result, the expanded uncertainty of real and imaginary part of impedance were 0.56 Ω and 0.57 Ω at 5.8 GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: Identification and correction of artefact in the measurement of pulsed magnetic fields
abstract: AC magnetic flux density meters usually integrate a high pass filter with a very low cut-off frequency (1 Hz-30 Hz) aiming at reducing the effect of slow oscillations. This can distort the actual time domain behaviour of induction waveforms detectable close to industrial or medical devices, even causing artefact high amplitude oscillations. This paper proposes a procedure to identify the filter parameters that accurately reproduce its measured frequency behaviour and suggests an algorithm to correct, in time domain, the field meter recorded waveform.

articleTitle: The METAS watt balance Mark II
abstract: The watt balance Mark II of the Federal Institute of Metrology METAS is ready to start the measurement of the Planck constant. After an intensive conception phase, the different modules of the experiment have been designed, realized and characterized in close collaboration with external partners. Beside an overview of the experimental setup and some results, the present paper shows also theoretical aspects and simulation results of the magnetic circuit. First results of the Planck constant should be available at the time of the conference.

articleTitle: Direct comparison of fractional and integer quantized Hall resistances: Status and perspectives
abstract: The direct comparison of fractional and integer quantized Hall resistances with metrological accuracy is of fundamental interest. With respect to the measurement instrumentation, this is a demanding experiment requiring the use of a cryogenic current comparator at very low current levels. We discuss settings and results of a comparison between the resistances for filling factors of 1/3 or of 2, respectively, and consider further improvements.

articleTitle: Towards the next generation NPL watt balance
abstract: To gain the maximum benefit from the forthcoming redefinition of the SI unit of mass, the kilogram, there is a need for an accurate but relatively simple-to-operate method of realising mass from the new definition. Recent advances in the theory and methods of operation of watt balances have made it possible to consider building a next generation of watt balances to fulfill this need. The paper summarises the recent advances and describes the path NPL intends to take to produce a new design of watt balance which is aimed at the routine realisation of SI mass.

articleTitle: Improvements on the design of a four terminal-pair coaxial bridge
abstract: This paper describes how recent modifications made at the four terminal-pair coaxial bridge (4TCB), in operation at Inmetro, have improved the coaxiality of the bridge, significantly reducing the net current in the coaxial cables, thus reducing both electromagnetic noise and possible systematic errors. This has improved the reliability and repeatability of impedance measurements, and has enabled us to achieve uncertainties as low as parts in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup>.

articleTitle: Metrological connector conversion technique for scattering parameter calibration
abstract: This paper proposes a connector conversion technique for coaxial lines using an original adaptor up to 100 MHz. The adaptor does not contain an insulator bead between the inner and the outer conductor. Scattering parameter (S-parameter) of the adaptor was calculated from the dimensional measurement results. For verification of the method, we applied it to Type N50 to 3.5 mm adaptor. It is because the S-parameter standards for the two connectors have been already developed at NMIJ. In phase measurement, the maximum difference between the calibrated and calculated value was less than the calibration uncertainty. The method provided reasonable results.

articleTitle: A proposal to establish a system for calibration of harmonic power analyzers
abstract: A proposal to establish a system for calibration of harmonic power analyzers is discussed, including its test protocol of calibration test points and other relevant considerations.

articleTitle: The new kilogram materialized by silicon isotopes
abstract: The Physikalisch-Technische Bundesanstalt (PTB) is currently elaborating a concept for the maintenance and dissemination of the SI unit kilogram on the basis of silicon spheres. For this purpose, handling procedures and work instructions are elaborated. These contain the realisation of the redefined kilogram by means of <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">28</sup>Si spheres and <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nat</sup>Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">qp</sub> spheres as primary respectively “quasi primary” mass measurement standards and disseminated with industrially manufactured <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nat</sup>Si<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sc</sub> spheres as secondary mass measurement standards. The described procedures are to be developed in cooperation with industrial partners.

articleTitle: The construction of the new Joule balance at the NIM
abstract: The Joule balance method is one of the several approaches to measure the Planck constant for the redefinition kilogram. The first prototype has been built to check the feasibility of the principle and the relative uncertainty is 2.6×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−6</sup>. To get better result and make contribution for the redefinition, since 2013, a new Joule balance has been designed with several new approaches to decrease the main uncertainty contributions in the first prototype. In 2015, the new joule balance has been mounted and some rough measurements have been done in air for the fine adjustment and alignment in the near future.

articleTitle: Thickness measurements of oxide and carbonaceous layer on a 28Si sphere by using XPS
abstract: Surface layer characterization is crucial for high-accuracy determination of the Avogadro constant by using <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">28</sup>Si enriched spheres for redefinition of the kilogram. In this work, we carried out the thickness measurements of the oxide and carbonaceous layer on a <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">28</sup>Si-enriched sphere by x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) for a pilot study to confirm the international equivalence of the ability to realize the kilogram from the new definition. A sphere rotation mechanism was installed into the XPS system to measure the thickness at different points on the surface. The average thickness and uncertainty budget of the oxide and carbonaceous layers were evaluated.

articleTitle: Towards an impedance bridge based on a single programmable Josephson voltage standard
abstract: This paper describes the work made at CEM in order to develop an impedance bridge based on a single programmable Josephson voltage standard. Advantages and limitations of this approach are analyzed and compared with bridges based on two Josephson voltage standards.

articleTitle: A two thickness interferometer for lattice strain investigations
abstract: We describe a test carried out by using a two-thickness interferometer to investigate the effect of the surface stress on the measurement of the silicon lattice constant.

articleTitle: AC-DC current transfer standards suitable for use below 1 mA and up to 1 MHz
abstract: Traceability for AC currents below 1 mA is needed to calibrate calibrators and multimeters at frequencies up to at least 100 kHz. Since the sensitivity of thermal convertors is not sufficient, only transfer standards using amplifiers are suitable. A newly designed combination of an amplifier and a shunt works at higher frequencies up to 1 MHz as well.

articleTitle: The frequency dependence of a 10 nF gas-dielectric capacitor
abstract: A direct realization of the farad from the quantum Hall effect involve the comparison of the Hall resistance with a capacitor, using a dedicated impedance bridge. Best measurement uncertainty is achieved for frequencies not corresponding to the traditional ones employed in dissemination (1 kHz, or 10 krad s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>). Hence, standards having a known frequency dependence are necessary to perform a correction. Here we investigate, with network analysis techniques, the frequency dependence of a new commercial 10 nF gas-dielectric capacitance standard.

articleTitle: AC quantum Hall effect in epitaxial graphene
abstract: This paper describes measurements of the AC quantum Hall resistance in epitaxial graphene performed with a newly developed digitally assisted impedance bridge. Capacitive losses cause a negative frequency dependence of the quantum Hall resistance, in contrast to the positive frequency dependence observed in GaAs devices. The magnitude of the frequency dependence varies among individual graphene samples and can be significantly larger than in GaAs devices.

articleTitle: Comparison of calibration methods for multiport VNAs up to 67 GHz
abstract: In this paper two multiport calibration schemes for vector network analyzer (VNA) characterization, including port-to-port and full multiport procedures, are compared with regard to underlying error models and measurement results. Test measurements have been performed, using a 4-port VNA. As device under test (DUT), a 3-port power splitter was employed, with the remaining VNA test-port being short-circuited and utilized to examine port isolation. Additional verification measurements were performed at NPL and LNE.

articleTitle: Recent improvements of NICT atomic fountains CsF1 & CsF2
abstract: NICT atomic fountains CsF1 and CsF2 and their frequency reference based on a cryogenic sapphire oscillator (CSO) are being upgraded with aiming at operations at the low 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-16</sup> level. The CSO was upgraded from “dewar-type” to “cryocooler-type” and a long-term continuous operation became available without routine liquid helium transfer. A rapid adiabatic passage method was installed to the fountain in order to correct for a collision shift precisely. The temperature control for the main chamber started to reduce uncertainties of shifts related to the blackbody radiation and the microwave cavity. Other improvements are being undertaken.

articleTitle: Scaling the current from a GHz electron pump using a CCC
abstract: We demonstrate the scaling of the current from a tunable-barrier electron pump using a cryogenic current comparator (CCC) with a turns ratio of 1:22592. The amplified current flows in a calibrated 100 kΩ resistor, and the voltage drop across this resistor is directly compared against a binary Josephson array. The experimental setup constitutes a prototype realization of the metrology triangle proposed more than 15 years ago.

articleTitle: Four terminal pair digital sampling impedance bridge
abstract: This paper describes digital sampling bridge for impedance measurement up to few tens of kHz in four terminal pair definition. It is primarily dedicated for low impedance measurements with comparison currents over 10 A however it can be used at least up to few tens of kΩ as well. Achieved uncertainty for near unity impedance ratio is few μΩ/Ω and the phase angle uncertainty at 1 kHz is few μrad (coverage factor k = 2). Due to the used signal processing method the bridge can be used even for sub-10mV voltage drops on the standards.

articleTitle: Expansion of the measurement range of AC shunt resistor standard
abstract: There has been a demand for accurate measurements of ac shunt resistors with a nominal value of 1 mS or less for both in-phase and quadrature components. Thus, to expand the ranges of impedance and frequency of the calibration system for ac shunt resistors, a current bridge method with cascaded current transformers (CTs) has been developed. An ac shunt resistor with nominal value of 10 mS was evaluated by a current bridge method using cascaded CTs, and the results of the calibration system using this method were validated. It was found that the calibration system for ac shunt resistors using the current-bridge method with cascaded CTs can be used successfully for both in-phase and quadrature components up to 3 kHz.

articleTitle: Advanced applications of AMR data to generate functions for enhancing SMART GRID operation
abstract: Automatic Meter Reading (AMR) coupled with Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) are enabling technologies to allow their advanced applications to generate functions for enhancing SMART GRID operation. The application of these technologies and their traceability issues, including their corresponding functions, for enhancing SMART GRID operation will be presented at the conference.

articleTitle: Pre-stabilization of a distributed feedback diode laser for locking to a high-finesse cavity
abstract: An ultra-stable laser based on frequency doubling of a distributed feedback (DFB) semiconductor laser has been built for interrogation of the 674-nm clock transition in Sr<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>. The DFB laser is pre-stabilized using an all-fiber interferometer that reduces the linewidth from the 1 MHz regime down to a few kHz and enables reliable locking of the laser to a 30-cm reference cavity with a finesse of 270 000 at 674 nm The laser will be used in a Sr<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> single-ion clock that should reach a fractional frequency uncertainty of a few parts in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-18</sup>.

articleTitle: Dissipation factor and frequency dependence of graphene quantum Hall devices
abstract: Quantum Hall resistors made from epitaxial graphene measured with alternating current exhibit an unusual negative frequency dependence. To test the hypothesis that parasitic capacitances between contact pads cause this effect, we studied capacitance and dissipation factor in the quantum Hall regime for various in-plane electrode configurations. The largest dissipation factor is found for configurations where a strong electric field penetrates the bulk of the graphene. The measured effect of different electrode configurations on the frequency dependence of the quantized Hall resistance confirms our hypothesis. The findings are important for modeling and optimization of a future graphene-based quantum impedance standard.

articleTitle: Error estimation of magnetic flux measurement of the permanent magnet materials in an open magnetic circuit
abstract: This paper presents results of experiments in an open magnetic circuit by designing a magnetic flux measurement setup which consists of self-adhesive coils without frames: the leakage magnetic flux which exists between the coil and the permanent magnet is the main source of errors. It's shown that the coil should have the greater width, the thinner thickness, smaller diameter and the coils should be close to the permanent magnet to minimize the errors. Meanwhile, it's shown that the velocity of sample passing through the coil doesn't affect the results.

articleTitle: Error correction: A proposal for a standard
abstract: Some of the errors in transducers such as instrument transformers can be corrected as part of the digital processing for the measurement. The instrument transformer can be characterized in such a way that allows the Transducer Electronic Data Sheet of IEEE Std 1451 to transfer the information to the measurement system. A modification would allow the measurement system to perform a high-quality self-calibration whenever a transducer was replaced. That levies requirements on the characterization accuracy of the instrument transformer.

articleTitle: Self-calibration of the current comparator with common ground
abstract: A method to measure the phase angle errors and amplitude errors of the current comparators with ratio of 2:1, 5:1 and 10:1 has been described. The method is based on the use of the differential current transformer to determine the current relationship of the current comparator. The measurements have been done at frequencies from 10 kHz to 100 kHz, and the results are presented.

articleTitle: Packaging of fiber-coupled module for Josephson junction array voltage standards
abstract: This paper describes issues related to the packaging of a fiber coupled optoelectronic module intended as a current source for pulse-driven Josephson arrays, operating at cryogenic temperatures. The module consists of flip-chip bonded photodiodes on a silicon carrier with adhesively bonded optical fiber components in a compact package. Optical and thermomechanical simulations were performed, showing that the needed functionality can be achieved, with optical coupling efficiency above 90% for fiber-chip misalignments up to 40 μm, and that the thermomechanical stresses can be reduced by controlling of the adhesive bonding process.

articleTitle: Asynchronous 3-phase power measurements
abstract: A new asynchronous, 3-phase/4-channel Power Analyzer for high precision analysis of AC voltage, AC current and power. Advanced signal processing algorithms provide precise measurements of single period events (i.e. single period of a wave form) for sinusoidal, non-sinusoidal and quasi-stationary signals. The uncertainty for AC current and power measurements of a single period event are <;75 pμ/A and <;200 μW/W. The uncertainty of the phase measurement between two single period events (i.e. voltage-to-voltage, current-to-current, and voltage-to-current) is <;50 μrad. Uncertainties are materially reduced with averaging over multiple periods. This paper describes the architecture and algorithms.

articleTitle: Microwave radiometry of blackbody radiation
abstract: We outline the theoretical formulation of radiometry of the free-space radiation emitted by a blackbody target. Simulation shows a much smaller drop of radiation intensity of a Lambertian source than that of an incoherent source in the near-field region, indicative of a powerful influence produced by the coherence property of the blackbody source. Further, the coupling of the radiation to a radiometer is formulated by the plane-wave scattering theory of the radiation field.

articleTitle: Quasi coherent overlapping procedure to improve harmonics suppression using single tone estimation algorithms
abstract: This paper describes the procedure to reduce an estimation bias of interpolated DFT and single-model sine-fit algorithms. Estimation bias reduction of more than an order of magnitude is attainable. The procedure does not modify the estimation algorithm itself and additional knowledge of the measurement system or additional sampled points are not required.

articleTitle: Geomagnetic measurement and analysis of Cheongyang observatory
abstract: Cheongyang (CYG) observatory conducted two modes of geomagnetic measurement: absolute measurements for deriving the baseline values and continuous measurement of geomagnetic field variation. Measurements are made using high accuracy vector and scalar magnetometers and non-magnetic theodolite in accordance with the INTERMAGNET (International Real-time Magnetic Observatory Network) specifications. The baseline values obtained from the absolute measurements are fitted using piecewise polynomials of order 3 or less from which the final baseline values are calculated. Variations of less than 5 nT was observed in all the components of the geomagnetic field which is within INTERMAGNET requirement.

articleTitle: Use of a nanocrystalline core for a precise non-invasive AC current measurement
abstract: An apparatus working on current transformer with split nanocrystalline core principle is described in the paper. It enables non-invasive measurement of AC current at frequency band of 50 Hz to 7 kHz. Ratio error and phase displacement do not exceed 0.12 % and 35' at transformation ratio of 500 A/1 A, real secondary burden of 3 Ω and secondary current range of (1-120) %. The ratio error does not substantially change and phase displacement does not exceed the value 220' at frequency range to 7 kHz.

articleTitle: Uncertainty improvement of monopole antenna calibration using equivalent capacitance substitution method
abstract: In this paper a method to improve the measurement uncertainty from the inaccurate representation of the equivalent capacitance of a short monopole antenna element is proposed for the equivalent capacitance substitution method (ECSM). And some consideration about the model formula of the effective height of a monopole antenna is also discussed.

articleTitle: A three-phase calibration and field measurement setup based on a custom digitizer
abstract: This paper describes a new three-phase power measurement setup to be used as a national power standard in Finland. A custom 6-channel digitizer was previously developed for the purpose together with measurement software, which can be extended at will to accommodate new analyses. The setup can easily be moved outside the lab for field measurements. Voltage attenuators are custom-made at VTT and different types of current sensors can be selected for use depending on current levels and location. Uncertainty budget is currently being made for the setup.

articleTitle: Tests on waveform synthesis in a new cryocooler setup
abstract: A new experimental setup based on a two-stage cryocooler has been developed at INRIM for operation with Josephson arrays. Recently some parts of the setup have been upgraded in order to allow the synthesis of waveforms; in particular, a well suited rigid rf coaxial cable with bandwidth exceeding 30 GHz has been mounted. We describe preliminary results obtained in tests of waveform synthesis with pulse-driven Josephson arrays fabricated at PTB. Unipolar sinewaves at 1.25 kHz and amplitudes ranging up to tens of millivolts were generated. Results are then discussed in relation with the specific thermal issues posed by He-free cooling.

articleTitle: Calibration of sample-time error in a sampling oscilloscope and uncertainty analysis
abstract: In this paper, we propose estimation methods for the sample-time errors using multiple quadrature signals. To confirm the estimator, we perform Monte-Carlo simulation. The result shows that the proposed methods provide reliable confidence interval while the ODRPACK with reference two channels increases the outage as the independent jitter of each sampler is increased.

articleTitle: Extending AC-DC current transfer to 100 A, 100 kHz in UME
abstract: This paper describes work in TÜBİTAK UME, National Metrology Institute of Turkey, on expanding ac current measurement capabilities to 100 A up to 100 kHz. In the scope of the work current shunts based on cage and coaxial foil design are produced. New high current shunts are compared with existing system at 20 A in a step-up procedure. Here is briefly presented design of the shunts and results of the comparison measurements.

articleTitle: A two-channel digital sampling system for estimating harmonic parameters at low frequencies developed at CENAMEP AIP
abstract: A two-channel digital sampling system for estimating harmonic parameters at low frequencies, which utilizes two integrating digital sampling voltmeters in a master-slave configuration, was developed at Centro Nacional de Metrología de Panamá (CENAMEP AIP). A bilateral study was then conducted between Instituto Nacional de Metrologia, Qualidade e Tecnologia (Inmetro) and CENAMEP AIP to compare the estimation results and to evaluate the symmetry of the two digitizing channels.

articleTitle: Establishing of 1000V multi-decade inductive voltage divider standard at NIM
abstract: A multi-decade inductive voltage divider (IVD) with special electric shielding is established at NIM as the highest standard in the field of ratio traceability system. A compensation method which is based on the principle of transformer is applied in this IVD to raise the accuracy. An improved bootstrap calibration method with triaxial guards is proposed, and a new type of reference transformer is designed to calibrate the multi-decade IVD in combination usage. The accuracy of this IVD is better than 0.05 μ V/V with the calibration uncertainty less than 0.01 μ V/V.

articleTitle: Comparison of two methods for determining the sorption correction for a vacuum-realized kilogram
abstract: The International System of Units (SI) is expected to be revised in 2018, and in this new system, the unit of mass, the kilogram, will be realized in a vacuum environment. In order to transfer the vacuum realization to artifacts in atmospheric pressure air, the effects of the sorption of atmospheric contaminants must either be corrected for or eliminated. NIST has constructed a system that directly compares a mass in vacuum to a mass in air, thereby eliminating the need for sorption correction. We describe the operation of this system and compare results to those obtained from sorption corrections.

articleTitle: Upgrading the NIST electrostatic force balance
abstract: After the adoption of a redefined SI, electrostatic force measurements will become an ideal way to realise forces at the sub-micronewton level in a laboratory setting using an instrument such as the NIST electrostatic force balance. The balance has recently undergone a complete replacement of the control system. We describe both the new updated control system and recent improvements to analysis and data collection.

articleTitle: Ultra-high resistance measurement based on non-contact electrostatic voltmeter
abstract: In order to overcome the drawback that the measurement uncertainty of the ultra-high resistance over 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</sup> Ω may be deteriorated severely due to insufficient resolution of the electrometer in conventional scheme, a novel method based on the dual sources high resistance bridge and non-contact voltage measurement is presented. The measurement uncertainty is largely dependent on the standard resistance and determined by the resolution of the electrostatic voltmeter. It is shown by the experimental results that the measurement uncertainty for the resistance of 100 TΩ to 1000 TΩ is better than 0.2%, k = 2.

articleTitle: The establishment of mA CT calibration system at KTL and comparison with NRC
abstract: mA CTs are not addressed by either IEC or IEEE standards. They are used in power/energy measurement systems in large apartment buildings or shopping centers. This paper describes the establishment of mA CT calibration system at KTL and its comparison with NRC.

articleTitle: Vector network analyzer comparison up to 110 GHz in 1 mm coaxial line
abstract: We present a measurement comparison between two Vector Network Analyzers (VNA) on 1 mm coaxial line up to 110 GHz. The first VNA uses broadband coaxial test head modules while the second is coaxial up to 67 GHz and uses waveguide test head modules from 67 GHz to 110 GHz, connected to 1 mm coaxial line through waveguide to coaxial adapters. This comparison is carried out in order to assess the level of confidence and to prepare the uncertainty budget in view of submitting new Measurement and Calibration Capabilities (CMCs) in the domain of S parameters measurements up to 110 GHz.

articleTitle: Mass measurement of 28Si-enriched spheres at NMIJ for determination of the Avogadro constant
abstract: The Avogadro constant is determined accurately by applying the x-ray crystal density method to <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">28</sup>Si-enriched spheres, which is one of the practical methods for the kilogram redefinition. In this paper, we present the results of mass measurements of <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">28</sup>Si-enriched spheres, performed at NMIJ in 2014 for the determination of the Avogadro constant. The results of reproducibility of the cleaning effects on the mass of the spheres together with the influence of the BIPM Extraordinary Calibrations, are shown. With these achievements, NMIJ plans to participate in the Pilot Study aiming at the kilogram redefinition, where the mass measurements play an important role.

articleTitle: Piston guide and magnet assembly for the KRISS watt balance
abstract: The piston guide and magnet assembly for the KRISS watt balance were tested. The velocity of the piston guide was controlled within 4×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup> at the velocity of 2 mm s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> using a linear motor and linear encoder feedback. The magnet assembly which consists of two permanent magnet rings and closed yokes was fabricated. B-field at the air gap of 25 mm was measured using a Hall probe. The B-field uniformity was within 5×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup> over the vertical distance of 24 mm.

articleTitle: Development of 1 Ω and 10 Ω metal foil standard resistors
abstract: We have been developing compact super-stable standard resistors raging from 1 Ω to 10 kΩ, and in this paper development and evaluation of 1 Ω and 10 Ω resistors are described. Typical drift rates of them are 0.1 μΩ/(Ω·year) or less. Temperature coefficients have been also evaluated for 10Ω resistors. These performances meet calibration laboratory conditions for maintenance of resistance standards and calibration services.

articleTitle: Nature never deals off of the bottom of the deck…but she holds all of the aces: The joys of doing precision measurement science
abstract: I will talk about the family of experiments known as precision measurement and null experiments. These experiments, often associated with the determination of a fundamental constant or the testing of one of the accepted laws of Nature at some extreme of magnitude, have always provided a challenge to both a scientist's cunning and his or her experimental skills. In my talk I will use as one example, C.V. Boys' 1894 measurement of big G. [C.V. Boys, one of my physics heroes, wrote papers that evidenced his humanity and sense of humor and are, accordingly, very enjoyable to read. Unfortunately, journal editors go to great lengths to remove from today's publications any hint of humanity, humor, or enjoyment derived from doing science.]

articleTitle: Plane mirror based method for laser beam alignment
abstract: This paper describes a method for laser beam alignment using plane mirror, which can be used in the watt/joule balance laser beam alignment. The mirror surface is calibrated by a vertical axis standard platform. An electrical level meter is used as readout unit and rotated on the platform. The plane mirror which is also on the rotation platform is then adjusted horizontal using laser and PSD readout. The experiment indicates that the vertical axis standard has the uncertainty of about 28μrad The incline of the plane mirror is estimated to about 3μrad.

articleTitle: High precision slotted cavity measurement of a novel ceramic state polymer electrolyte
abstract: In this paper, a special designed transverse slotted cavity is built in X-band to Ka-band. It was applied to determine the complex permittivity of a novel “ceramic state” polymer electrolytes by employing perturbation theory. The dielectric spectra of this material had been characterized. The complex alternating current electrical conductivity and the ionic conductivity can be deserved from the complex dielectric spectra.

articleTitle: Improvement of leakage resistance of PJVS for NIST-4 watt balance experiment
abstract: A Programmable Josephson Voltage Standard (PJVS) system is used for the voltage measurements in the NIST-4 watt balance experiment. In order to achieve the uncertainty of voltage measurements better than 1 part in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sup>, it is critical to increase the leakage resistance of the PJVS to ground. This paper describes how to modify the watt balance PJVS system to isolate the bias electronics and quantify its resistance to ground. Direct comparison between the watt balance PJVS (WPJVS) and NIST Volt Lab PJVS (VPJVS) was carried out to verify the performance of WPJVS with improved isolation resistance.

articleTitle: Universality test of the quantum Hall effect on topological insulator
abstract: Progress toward a universality test of the quantum Hall effect on topological insulator is presented. In order to measure the quantized Hall resistance on topological insulator precisely, it is critically important to reduce bulk carrier conduction. Therefore, S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>-doped Bi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.1</sub>Sb<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.9</sub>Te<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>S, a newly found topological insulator, was used for the measurement material, and its single crystals were exfoliated into thin flakes. The S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>-doped Bi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1.1</sub>Sb<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.9</sub>Te<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>S flakes are processed into measurement devices with multiple electrodes for four-probe measurement. Future prospects for the precise measurements using a cryogenic current comparator are also noted.

articleTitle: Bilateral comparison of RF power measurements with 2.4 mm connectors between SCL and NMC, A*STAR
abstract: This paper presents a bilateral comparison of RF power measurements with 2.4 mm connectors carried out between the National Metrology Centre of the Agency for Science, Technology and Research (NMC, A∗STAR) of Singapore and the Standards and Calibration Laboratory (SCL) of Hong Kong. The comparison demonstrates the precision measurement capabilities and validates the equivalence of coaxial power calibration services with 2.4 mm connectors at both the laboratories.

articleTitle: Methods for characterization and minimization of microwave background in cryogenic environment
abstract: Minimizing microwave background of cryogenic environment is crucial for quantum devices where single microwave photon energy is sufficient to disturb the measured system. Microwave photons with sufficient energy originate from the warmer parts of the cryostat, for example from parts at liquid helium temperature (4.2 K), which can be about three orders of magnitude higher than the sample temperature. Reduction of the microwave background is possible with careful design of both shielding and filtering of the sample holder. Additionally, on-chip filtering of the actual quantum device can improve the device performance significantly.

articleTitle: Digital control of magnetic induction waveform applied to silicon steel sheets characterization
abstract: This paper presents a new algorithm for controlling the magnetic induction waveform in a specific measurement system for the magnetic characterization and modeling of silicon steel sheets. Experimental results show that, with this new control algorithm, the measurement system is able to characterize silicon steel sheets under sinusoidal or nonsinusoidal waveforms in wide frequency and amplitude range.

articleTitle: Noise reductions in the NRC watt balance
abstract: After publication in 2014 of a Planck constant determination with low uncertainty [1], various modifications have been made to the NRC watt balance to lower type A and B uncertainty components. This paper lists the significant changes and in particular, details the reduction of the largest type A component by almost an order of magnitude. The impact of this reduction is then described with our first clear observation of the changes in the environmental magnetic flux density using the watt balance.

articleTitle: Comparison of two realisations of a power standard
abstract: The paper describes a comparison conducted at the National Measurement Institute Australia (NMIA) between the thermal power comparator that sets the Australian standard of power and the digital power comparator developed at the D. I Mendeleyev Institute for Metrology, Russia. The difference between the two systems did not exceed 5 μW/VA at 53 Hz, 240 V currents of 2.5 A and 4.5 A, and power factors from 0 to 1.

articleTitle: A preliminary magnet nonlinear research on the joule balance
abstract: The joule balance experiment has been carried out at the National Institute of Metrology, China (NIM) since 2007. To reduce the measurement uncertainty further, the major parts of the second generation of the joule balance apparatus system is built already. A new magnet system using electromagnet is being adopted to reduce self-heating in the coils. However the results on the measurement show that the nonlinearity and hysteresis of the ferromagnetic material will bring a considerable measurement uncertainty. In this paper, the nonlinear effect is reduced by one order of magnitude by an experimental method. The nonlinearity and hysteresis effect is about 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> in the relative standard uncertainty.

articleTitle: Thermoelectric power transfer standards for V- and W-band
abstract: Improved thermoelectric waveguide power standards covering the frequency range 50 GHz to 110 GHz are described. They are specially designed for primary high frequency power calibration in microcalorimeters to provide traceability with lowest uncertainty. Design, experimental results, and comparison with conventional thermistor power sensors are presented.

articleTitle: Concentricity alignment between electromagnet yoke and suspended coil in NIM-2
abstract: The concentricity alignment error between the electromagnet yoke and the suspended coil is one of the key undetermined sources of Planck constant measured by Joule Balance NIM-2. Firstly, three capacitance sensors are mounted on the frame of the suspended coil with 120° equal angular distribution to measure the concentricity alignment errors. Secondly, the theoretical model of the concentricity alignment error is built. Finally, the concentricity alignment error is measured by experiments. Experimental and theoretical results show that the concentricity error is 17μm which meets the alignment requirement of Joule Balance NIM-2.

articleTitle: Development of a NIST WR10 radiometer
abstract: This paper describes the development of a waveguide radiometer to measure noise from millimeter wave electronic components from 75 GHz to 110 GHz. The radiometer will estimate the noise temperature of a device under test (DUT) based on comparison with room temperature and 77K noise standards. This is a standard physical approach in other NIST microwave radiometers. The radiometer is particularly amenable to performing noise temperature as well as noise parameter measurements for amplifier and transistor characterization. As wireless communications progresses towards millimeter wave systems, noise characterization of related components and subsystems becomes essential. We report our progress in radiometer design, construction and verification for millimeter wave noise metrology at NIST.

articleTitle: Millimeter-sized graphene quantum hall devices for resistance standards
abstract: We present a repeatable process to produce millimeter-sized graphene device for quantum Hall resistance (QHR) standard. Our large-area, homogeneous monolayer graphene is grown on silicon carbide (SiC) substrate at high temperature by an optimized epitaxial method. Well-developed quantum Hall plateaus have been observed in devices fabricated from samples annealed at 1900 <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>C by a clean lithography process. Metrological accuracy of better than 5 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-9</sup> has been observed in a 27 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, octagonal device at a record current level of 0.72 mA for temperatures between 1.6 K and 3.1 K.

articleTitle: A direct DC 10 V comparison between the NIMJ and the BIPM Programmable Josephson Voltage Standards
abstract: An NMIJ Programmable Josephson Voltage Standard (PJVS) and the new BIPM transportable PJVS based on a NIST array have been directly compared at 10 V. The results show an excellent relative agreement of 5×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-12</sup> within a total relative combined uncertainty of better than 1×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-10</sup>. The low side of the NMIJ array is always connected to the reference potential of the measurement setup; therefore we have investigated on possible systematic errors due to the leakage resistance to ground (LRG). The results show that a compromise should be found on the NMIJ PJVS between the noise at the output of the measurement leads, related width of the quantum voltage step and voltage systematic error related to the LRG. The number of capacitances across the measurement leads has a direct impact on the systematic error introduced by the LRG Furthermore the isolation resistance of the selected capacitances must be carefully measured.

articleTitle: Static phase improvements in the LNE watt balance
abstract: This paper describes some mechanical and electrical improvements in the LNE watt balance experiment. A new single-piece balance beam has been developed and the electrical system to servo-control its equilibrium position during the static phase has been modified.

articleTitle: VRC measurement for 3.5 mm one-port coaxial system using network analyzer fitted with Type K connector
abstract: This paper describes Voltage Reflection Coefficient (VRC) measurement for 3.5 mm one-port coaxial system using network analyzer fitted with Type K connector by incorporating measurement uncertainty due to discontinuity between the two different connector types. Connector simulation models were made and the discontinuity was analyzed by finite element method. Maximum VRC deviation in the presence of the discontinuity was simulated to estimate the measurement uncertainty in accordance with GUM. VRC Measurement for some 3.5 mm loads was made to verify the uncertainty component due to this discontinuity.

articleTitle: SIM key comparison of 10 mH inductance standards
abstract: A key comparison of 10 mH inductance standards at 1 kHz has been carried out with the participation of seven National Metrology Institutes (NMI's) of the Inter-American Metrology System (SIM), within the frame of the International Committee for Weights and Measures Mutual Recognition Arrangement (MRA), which was piloted by CENAM, Mexico. Three previously characterized commercial inductors, contained in individual enclosures with controlled temperature were used as traveling standards. This paper presents the results and technical details of the comparison.

articleTitle: Towards a cryogen-free table-top primary resistance standard
abstract: We demonstrate quantum Hall resistance measurements with metrological accuracy in a small cryogen-free system operating at a temperature of around 3.8 K and magnetic fields below 5 T. We use this system to investigate the optimisation of graphene/SiC devices for maximum breakdown current. In addition we report the first characterisation of a cryogen-free cryogenic current comparator which enables entirely cryogen-free primary resistance metrology.

articleTitle: Laser refractometer as a transfer standard of the pascal
abstract: We have developed a new low pressure sensor which is based on the measurement of (nitrogen) gas refractivity inside a Fabry-Perot (FP) cavity. We compare pressure determinations via this laser refractometer to that of well-established ultrasonic manometers throughout the range 100Pa to 100000Pa. The refractometer demonstrates 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> precision for p > 50 kPa; - as good or better than the manometer - we argue that a laser refractometer represents a state-of-the-art transfer standard of the pascal. We also claim the refractometer has an accuracy of U(p<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">FP</sub>) = [(16mPa)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> + (11.9 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> · p)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>]<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sup>, as realized through the properties of nitrogen gas.

articleTitle: Progress toward a new implementation of an In+ optical clock
abstract: Recent progress in implementing an In<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> optical clock based on an In<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> sympathetically-cooled with Ca<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> is reported. Our new implementation is expected to achieve a frequency uncertainty bellow the order of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−17</sup> as well as a future extension to a multi-ion optical clock with enhanced stability. Direct detection of an In<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> in a linear trap with Lamb-Dicke confinement using the <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup>P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> transition at 230 nm is successfully demonstrated, which enables the clock operation of the system.

articleTitle: Universality of the tunable-barrier electron pump at the part-per-million level
abstract: We summarize the results of precision measurement campaigns on semiconductor tunable-barrier electron pumps undertaken at NPL, over the last 5 years. We have investigated pumps of 3 different designs, fabricated in GaAs and silicon and operated on the 1-electron plateau at frequencies from 230 MHz to 1 GHz. For all measurements we find the pump current equal to e×f within the ≈1 ppm standard uncertainty of the current measurement. This accumulated data strongly suggests that accurate quantized operation of the tunable-barrier pump is a universal property, insensitive to the detailed design of the device. The data includes previously unpublished results.

articleTitle: Measurement of conductivity of materials at PTB
abstract: In research and industry, the determination of material parameters plays an important role. One of these parameters is the electrical conductivity σ. In metallic materials, it allows the purity of the raw metal and the correct composition of alloys to be checked. Due to increasing demand, PTB has decided to establish calibration facilities for semiconducting material. The measurement set-up and the new calibration facilities are described in this paper, including an uncertainty analysis.

articleTitle: Modelling of PMU uncertainty by means of Monte Carlo method
abstract: The Phasor Measurement Unit (PMU) simulator is presented in this paper. The aim of the simulator is to calculate the uncertainty of a PMU by means of the Monte Carlo method. A whole measurement chain is modeled in the simulator, including a transducer, a digitizer and a synchrophasor estimating algorithm. As an example of results of the simulator a total vector error of the modeled PMU is shown together with calculated uncertainty.

articleTitle: Comparison of mean diameters of silicon spheres measured with both spherical fizeau-interferometers of the PTB
abstract: The sphere interferometer 2 of the PTB was set up to undercut the measurement uncertainty already reached by the sphere interferometer 1 of the PTB. This was necessary for being able to meet the conditions of the CCM for a redefinition of the SI-unit kilogram where the sphere interferometers are used to measure the volume of the Avogadro spheres. This paper summarizes the comparison measurements between both interferometers and their results.

articleTitle: Quantum projection noise limited stability and blackbody radiation shift uncertainty of NRC's Sr+ atomic clock
abstract: We present the current status of the Sr<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> optical atomic ion clock at the National Research Council of Canada including the study of the quantum projection noise (QPN) limited stability and the progress on the evaluation of the blackbody radiation (BBR) shift uncertainty. The latest QPN limited stability of NRC's Sr+ clock is 3 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-15</sup> at 1 sec averaging time. The fractional evaluated accuracy of the Sr+ ion clock has reached 1.2 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-17</sup> and is now dominated by the BBR shift uncertainty, the improved evaluation of which is currently in progress.

articleTitle: Sub-Doppler laser spectroscopy of molecular iodine at 578 nm
abstract: We carry out sub-Doppler laser spectroscopy of hyperfine components of rovibrational transitions of molecular iodine at 578 nm using second harmonic generation of an 1156-nm external-cavity diode laser. The absolute frequencies of the hyperfine components can be determined by using an optical frequency comb to referenced to the Coordinated Universal Time of the National Metrology Institute of Japan. The hyperfine components at 578 nm can be good frequency references for the <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sub> clock transition in atomic ytterbium.

articleTitle: Method of displacement determination in calculable capacitor at NIM
abstract: This paper presents the displacement determination of the guard electrode for the new vertical calculable capacitor at NIM. We take a new method for measuring the displacement by actively locking the Fabry-Perot interferometer to a stabilized laser at two cavity lengths of interest. For each of the cavity lengths, the Fabry-Perot interferometer is maintained at its resonance, and the corresponding capacitance of the calculable capacitor is accurately measured by a capacitance bridge. Compared with the classic two-beam interferometer, this displacement-sensing system requires no fringe-counting unit, and is more suitable for the calculable capacitor.

articleTitle: Inmetro's coaxial calculable resistance project

authors.preferredName: Renata T. de Barros e Vasconcellos

abstract: This work describes experiments on the feasibility of a mechanical support for the resistive element of a calculable resistor. Construction issues involved in the project of the resistor are discussed.

articleTitle: Study of contact resistance in connectors with physical simulation using nano-fabrication
abstract: Contact resistance of electrical contact in connectors consists of constriction resistance that results from narrowing current and film resistance of high resistivity material between two electrodes. Constriction resistance depends on the number of contact points and their sizes. In the case of a simplified single point contact, the constriction resistance can be calculated analytically, however it is not the case for a real contact. To establish a relationship between the physical structure of an electrical contact and its constriction resistance, samples that represent the contact-simulated structure have been fabricated on a Si-chip for the measurements analysis of the constriction resistance.

articleTitle: Quantum based RF E-field sensing by using two-photon transition in Rydberg atoms
abstract: It has been proved that quantum coherence effects in highly-excited Rydberg atoms could provide a revolutionary solution for RF field measurement. A two-photon transition due to interaction of RF electric field with cesium Rydberg atoms will be discussed. RF E-field whose carrier frequency satisfies a two-photon transition can induce an Autler-Townes splitting within electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) spectroscopy, and the field strength is directly linked to the measured energy splitting and Planck's constant. Proof-of-concept measurement results will be presented, which also indicate the possibility of sub-wavelength sensing. This work is of major significance for developing quantum-based RF field metrology.

articleTitle: Making low level AC voltage measurements with DVM
abstract: The paper describes a method for the measurement of small alternating voltages, from 20 nV to 20 mV and higher, at frequencies up to 400 Hz. Particular attention is given to measurement at frequencies close but not equal to that of the mains. An application of the developed method to the characterization of reference current-to-voltage converters based on multistage current transformers is considered.

articleTitle: Towards a programmable quantum current generator
abstract: We report on the development of a programmable quantum current generator (PQCG) based on quantum voltage and resistance standards. First measurements with a digital amperemeter in the 100 μA range demonstrate the linearity of the generated current as a function of the theoretical current, linked to the electron charge, with a relative uncertainty of 2.7 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-7</sup> (k = 1). To overcome the detector limits and validate the PQCG as a practical realization of the ampere in the new SI, accurate quantization measurements with a target combined uncertainty of a few parts in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup> are in progress.

articleTitle: An improved sine function compensation algorithm in AC programmable Josephson voltage standard
abstract: An improved sine function compensation algorithm is described in AC programmable Josephson voltage standard. First, two methods, Average-DFT and DFT-Average, are analyzed in AC voltage magnitude calculation. Then some simulations and actual measurement experiment results are reported to interpret its accuracy.

articleTitle: Improvement of chemical vapor deposition graphene for quantum Hall resistance standards
abstract: Quantum Hall (QH) standard devices based on chemical vapor deposition (CVD) graphene have not shown properties as excellent as the one based on epitaxial graphene on SiC. This is because of the impurity, defects and inhomogeneity. In this paper, we demonstrate the progress on improving the quality of CVD graphene by the surface acidic processing and the low oxygen growth procedure.

articleTitle: Automated setup for calibration of calibrators at alternating voltage and alternating current
abstract: Calibrators are compact devices generating reference values for voltage, current, resistance and other quantities and are mainly used to calibrate measuring devices. Especially for AC quantities, there are wide parameter ranges for the generated values and frequencies, so that the traceable calibration of calibrators is a challenge. Different approaches have been investigated in order to design an automated setup to offer a calibration service for calibrators.

articleTitle: ‘Cutoff frequency’ of quantum-dot single-electron pump
abstract: We have investigated a ‘cut-off frequency’ f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf> beyond which the quantized charge pumping phenomena disappear in a quantum-dot (QD) pump. We have observed a shift of fc in the opposite direction to that of δ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> parameter, the figure of merit for the current-plateau flatness, depending on the potential profiles of the QD which can be controlled by a plunger gate. In relation with f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf>, we discuss the level-shift rate of a QD quasibound state in a nonadiabtic pumping phase.

articleTitle: Laser spectroscopy of muonic deuterium: New contribution to the proton puzzle
abstract: We report the first laser spectroscopy of muonic deuterium. At the Paul Scherrer Institute, we have measured the frequency of the 2S-2P Lamb shift in muonic deuterium. As in the case of the muonic hydrogen, the observed lines are shifted from the theoretical predictions. Thanks to improved new QED and nuclear structure calculations, an accurate determination of the deuteron radius can be extracted from our study. This determination will give a new and important input to the proton size puzzle.

articleTitle: Nanoradian angle measurements using differential Fabry-Perot interferometer
abstract: In this work, the novel angle measurement method that make use of Differential Fabry — Perot Interferometer (DFPI) and the High Precision Small Angle Generator (HPSAG) will be introduced. The DFPI using the frequency stabilized lasers and beat frequency measurement techniques was applied to the detection of ultra-small angles in the level of sub-nanoradian precision. During the application down to 1 nrad angular steps within the measurement range of 0.5 arcsec (2500 nrad) were generated using the HPSAG and these steps were detected by the DFPI which could measure angular displacements with picometer sensitivity free from linearity errors.

articleTitle: S parameters measurement of antennas under thermal stress
abstract: This paper highlights a process allowing both to establish and to quantify the temperature impact on the electromagnetic measurements in field emission between 2 antennas. We show the fabrication conditions of a radome in order to package one of the antennas, in order to vary the temperature inside the thermal chamber from 0°C to 50°C [1]. The results show the temperature influence on the electromagnetic properties of antenna and highlight the difficulty to get a thermal isotropy inside of radome.

articleTitle: Stepwise waveform generation using Josephson voltage standards for joule balance
abstract: The Flux linkage difference measurement is one of the key techniques in the joule balance with an electromagnet using ferromagnetic material. An arbitrary stepwise compensation waveform is needed to offset the induced voltage of the suspended coil with the finite rise/fall times. In this paper, the transitions of the induced voltage are respectively divided into 12 and 120 steps, and then processed to the PJVS with the purpose of synthesizing the desired transition for the compensation voltage. The result confirms that the PJVS has the capability to generate an arbitrary stepwise compensation voltage to offset the induced voltage.

articleTitle: High resolution spectroscopy of 1S-3S transition in hydrogen
abstract: The aim of our experiment is to improve the spectroscopy of atomic hydrogen in order to determine the charge radius of the proton. A new continuous laser source at 205 nm allows us to reach a statistical uncertainty of 2.2 kHz on the measurement of the 1S-3S transition frequency. This uncertainty could be sufficient to clarify the proton radius puzzle, however there remain systematic effects that are currently under study.

articleTitle: Precision measurements of quantum hall resistance plateau in doping-controlled graphene device
abstract: We report preliminary results of precision measurements of the graphene quantum Hall resistance plateau value with respect to magnetic field, temperature and applied current. Resistance value of SiC graphene Hall device was modulated by chemical doping, heating, and UV irradiation at the ambient condition. Precision measurements for Rh (filing factor v = 2) were then performed with a cryogenic current comparator resistance bridge. Relative deviation from R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">H</sub> (v = 2) less than 30 parts in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sup> can be achieved down to 7 T of magnetic field and up to 6 K of temperature with driving current of 19. 37 μA.

articleTitle: Quantum-based voltage metrology with superconducting Josephson devices at NIST
abstract: Over the past three decades, the quantum behavior of Josephson junctions has been exploited to improve the accuracy of dc voltage measurements by five orders of magnitude. State-of-the-art precision voltage-standard systems based on arrays of superconductive Josephson junctions can now provide quantum-accurate, intrinsically stable, programmable voltages at amplitudes greater than 10 V for dc voltages and up to 2 V rms for synthesized ac voltages such as sine waves and arbitrary waveforms. Various measurement techniques have been developed for ac measurement applications in the audio-frequency regime and for 60 Hz power metrology. I describe the key developments in Josephson circuits and in measurement techniques, and summarize their current performance and limitations for voltage metrology applications. In particular, I emphasize how the use of quantum-based systems, even when they produce apparently low-uncertainty and reproducible results, does not guarantee that the measurements are accurate. Finally, I briefly summarize how quantum-accurate, arbitrary waveform synthesis is being used to measure Boltzmann's constant by measuring the Johnson noise of a resistor at the triple-point of water, and how a practical electronic primary temperature standard might be realized with a quantum-based Johnson noise thermometer.

articleTitle: Improvements in the Inmetro Zener calibration uncertainty budgets using conventional and programmable Josephson Voltage Standards
abstract: This paper describes the réévaluation of Inmetro Conventional (CJVS) and Programmable (PJVS) Josephson Voltage Standards uncertainty budgets for Zener calibration. An intralaboratory indirect comparison between the two systems was made in order to check the consistency of the uncertainties. The achieved uncertainties are ±40 nV (at 1.018 V) and ±250 nV (at 10 V), k=2.

articleTitle: Frequency estimation of a damped sinusoidal signal and comparison to theoretical lower bound
abstract: Precision measurement of the frequency for a damped sinusoidal signal is important for fundamental symmetry test at the low energy scale. Here we analyzed the signal blockwisely and develop a model that can predict a correct blocksize dependence of the experimental frequency sensitivity. In addition, the model shows a leveling-off of the ultimate frequency precision beyond 2 times the damping time constant.

articleTitle: Precision μV-synthesizer based on a pulse-driven Josephson array
abstract: In this paper, we describe the development of a precision μV-synthesizer. The synthesizer is based on a pulse-driven Josephson array covering wide voltage and frequency ranges from nV to mV and DC to audio frequencies, respectively. We demonstrate 2-mA-wide current margins for the pulse-driven system and easy calibration of typical null detectors such as nanovoltmeters or lock-in amplifiers. Uncertainties at nV level can be achieved depending on the instruments used.

articleTitle: Proposal for a new quantum voltage standard based in optical frequency measurements
abstract: This paper presents a new method to measure the constant h/e based on optical measurements at room temperature. This could be a new quantum voltage standard alternative to present Josephson system

articleTitle: Development of single quantum Hall devices for the resistance standard in NIM
abstract: In this paper we report the progress on single quantum Hall devices for the resistance standards in NIM. We use the NIM-made device and the LEP-made device distributed to NIM by BIPM to calibrate a Tinsley 100 Ω transfer resistor using a cryogenic current comparator (CCC) at the filling factor k=2. The deviations of resistance values from the nominal value were -4.4808×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup>±3.5×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-9</sup> by NIM-1 and -4.4987×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup>±3.5×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-9</sup> by BIPM-2 separately. We assume the relative difference 1.8×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-8</sup> is due to the drift of the 100 Ω transfer resistor. More stable resistor will be used in future experiments.

articleTitle: Analysis of heat loss for measurement of Thomson coefficient using AC calorimetric method
abstract: We introduce an AC calorimetric technique to measure absolute Seebeck coefficient for thermoelectric metrology. The measurement of Thomson heat can only determine the Seebeck coefficient of single materials using Kelvin relation. Our heat transfer analysis in the Thomson heat measurement indicates that the use of AC current can compensate for the heat loss from the thermocouple, which is inevitable heat transfer in a contact temperature measurement. Experimental results nicely reproduce those predicted by the heat transfer analysis. Our AC calorimetric method allows us to perform accurate and simple measurements without considering the effect of heat loss.

articleTitle: Precision atom interferometry
abstract: Recent advances in atom optics and atom interferometry have enabled observation of atomic de Broglie wave interference when atomic wavepackets are separated by distances exceeding 50 cm and times of 2 seconds [1]. With further refinements, these methods may lead to meter-scale superpositions. In addition to providing new tests of quantum mechanics, these methods allow inertial force sensors of unprecedented sensitivity. We will describe methods demonstrated and results obtained in a 10 m atomic fountain configuration, their implications for technological applications in geodesy, and their relevance to fundamental studies in gravitational physics. We will describe how entangled atomic ensembles can be used to obtain further performance gains, following our demonstration of 18 dB measurement noise reduction using spin-squeezed atomic states [2].

articleTitle: Monitoring gravity for the NIST-4 watt balance
abstract: The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) new watt balance (NIST-4) has been constructed for the realization of mass through an exact value of the Planck constant in the new International System of Units (SI). The total relative uncertainty goal for the instrument of a few parts in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup> requires the determination of the local acceleration of gravity, g, with parts in 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sup> accuracy at the location of the mass at the time mechanical and electrical forces are being compared. We describe the procedures used and give results for the measurements of the local acceleration of gravity in the new watt balance facility.

articleTitle: Implementation of a programmable Josephson voltage standard in a zero boil-off dewar
abstract: MSL has successfully operated a programmable Josephson array system based on a NIST 2 V chip. The system is required for MSL's watt balance under development and involves a custom cryoprobe in a zero boil-off dewar. The design of the cryoprobe and its performance will be described. For example, at the optimum microwave power of 18.6 GHz and with all chip subarrays biased, a 1.34 mA step width of the quantized voltage was obtained at 4.25 K. In this mode the cryocooler maintained reserve cooling power of approximately 100 mW.

articleTitle: Calibration of 90° phase difference measured by digital sampling method
abstract: Digital sampling method is widely used in precision electromagnetic measurements based on DFT algorithms. The accuracy of phase difference measured by sampling method influences a lot to power, energy and so on. The active phase shifter is constructed to get stable 90° phase standard. To obtain the error of the phase shifter, two calibration steps are carried out in which a 1:-1 two-stage inductive voltage divider (IVD) is used. The calibration uncertainty for the 90° phase difference is 0.0006°. With the 90° phase standard, phase difference measured by a synchronous sampling digitizer using an improved DFT algorithm is calibrated.

articleTitle: Time-resolved detection of the Berry curvature in GaAs nanostructures
abstract: We optically induce a transient Berry curvature in GaAs quantum wells and detect it on a sub-picosecond time scale. Our results are important from two perspectives. First, they allow for local probing of the Berry curvature in energy and momentum space and, thus, might be used for new studies of the quantum Hall conductance which is equal to the integral of the Berry curvature over the Brillion zone. Second, they enable the study of important physical effects such as the spin Hall and anomalous Hall effects on ultrafast time scales.

articleTitle: Measurement comparison up to 65 GHz in coaxial 1.85 mm line
abstract: A measurement comparison of scattering parameters has been carried out between four national metrology laboratories in coaxial line using 1.85 mm precision connectors at frequencies between 100 MHz and 67 GHz. Twelve devices have been measured: two pairs of short-circuits, a pair of open-circuits, a pair of matched loads, a pair of mismatched loads, a male-to-female adaptor and a T-checker. The National Physical Laboratory (United Kingdom) acted as the pilot laboratory for the comparison.

articleTitle: Magnetocapacitance and dissipation factor of epitaxial graphene Hall bars
abstract: We report measurements of the magneto-capacitance and the associated dissipation factor of graphene-based quantum Hall effect devices at frequencies in the kHz range. The main motivation for this work is yielding information for the modeling and optimization of quantum Hall resistance devices measured with alternating current, but here we focus on the characteristic ac properties of graphene and the relevant loss mechanism.

articleTitle: Investigation of niobium nanoSQUIDs based on nanobridge junctions
abstract: NanoSQUIDs with Dayem nanobridge weak-link junctions were fabricated on single layer niobium film by focus ion beam(FIB) milling. The dimension of the nanobridge is less than 60 nm and the loop scale is from 400×400 nm to 2.5×20 μm. The working temperature range for this device was researched. The voltage-flux transfer properties were measured at different working temperatures.

articleTitle: Current status of terahertz frequency metrology at NICT
abstract: NICT has commenced development of an accurate and stable frequency standard for THz frequency band. We succeeded in phase-locking a single-mode 3THz quantum cascade laser (THz-QCL) to a THz reference. Using the phase-locked THz-QCL and a hot electron bolometer mixer, a THz wave generated by photomixing was evaluated. The result showed that the phase-locked THz-QCL and the optically generated THz wave had the same sability as the microwave references at the 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-15</sup> level and also that imposed noises during heterodyne mixing were negligibly small.

articleTitle: Progress of an atomic gravimeter at KRISS
abstract: This paper introduces an atomic gravimeter under development at KRISS for precise measurement of gravitational acceleration.
